description: Descriptive vs Reasoning questions for testing depth of figure understanding. Descriptive questions test visual reading (directly observable). Reasoning questions require inference, comparison, or judgment.
methodology: Each figure gets 2 descriptive + 2 reasoning questions. Answers scored as correct/incorrect. Compare descriptive-to-reasoning accuracy gap across models.

figures.ground_truth_context: 5 layer groups on x-axis, ~5 lines (LB-Avg, RULER4k variants, Baseline), y-axis is Relative Change (%), baseline at 0%

descriptive.question: How many distinct lines are shown in this figure?
descriptive.answer: 5 lines (LB-Avg of 2×tokens 8-bit, LB-Avg of 1×tokens 16-bit, RULER4k of 2×tokens 8-bit, RULER4k of 1×tokens 16-bit, Baseline of 4×tokens 4-bit)

descriptive.question: What is the approximate value of the lowest point across all lines?
descriptive.answer: Approximately -10% to -12%, occurring at Layer5-12 for one of the RULER4k lines

reasoning.question: Which configuration shows the most stable performance across all layer groups?
reasoning.answer: The Baseline (dashed line) stays near 0% across all groups, showing the most stable/flat performance

reasoning.question: Why do you think performance dips at Layer5-12 and then recovers? What does this pattern suggest about these layers?
reasoning.answer: This requires interpretation — the dip suggests these middle layers are most sensitive to the quantization/pruning, while early and late layers are more resilient. The recovery suggests later layers compensate.

figures.ground_truth_context: 6 slices: Frustration 25.1%, Neutral 23.1%, Anger 14.9%, Sadness 14.7%, Excitement 14.1%, Happiness 8.1%

descriptive.question: What are the two largest categories and their percentages?
What color is the smallest slice in the chart?

reasoning.question: Do negative emotions (Frustration, Anger, Sadness) collectively outweigh positive emotions (Happiness, Excitement)? By how much?
reasoning.answer: Negative: 25.1+14.9+14.7=54.7%. Positive: 8.1+14.1=22.2%. Negative outweighs by 32.5 percentage points.

reasoning.question: If this dataset were used for emotion recognition training, which emotions would likely have the worst classification accuracy and why?
reasoning.answer: Happiness (8.1%) would likely have worst accuracy due to severe class imbalance — too few training samples compared to Frustration/Neutral.

descriptive.question: How many bar groups are shown on the x-axis?
descriptive.answer: 6 groups (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics)

descriptive.question: Which specialty group has bars extending to the most negative values (lowest on the y-axis)?
descriptive.answer: Cardio, with the baseline bar reaching approximately -26.7

reasoning.question: For which specialty does fine-tuning produce the largest improvement over the baseline?
reasoning.answer: Requires comparing the gap between the light blue baseline bar and the fine-tuned bars across all groups. The specialty where fine-tuned bars are most different from baseline shows largest improvement.

reasoning.question: Does fine-tuning on a specialty's own data always produce the best result for that specialty, or do cross-specialty fine-tunes sometimes perform better?
reasoning.answer: Requires comparing within each group whether the same-color fine-tune bar is shortest (best). This is a nuanced cross-referencing task.

descriptive.answer: 两个y轴：左轴为每日新增患者人数(0-1,800,000)，右轴为新闻报道数(0-6,000)

reasoning.question: 新闻报道数量的变化是否与每日新增病例数同步？如果不同步，哪个领先？
reasoning.answer: 大致同步但存在滞后——病例高峰往往略早于报道高峰，说明媒体反应存在延迟

reasoning.question: 如果你是政策制定者，基于这张图你会在什么时间点开始加强防控措施？为什么？
